2: name: jetson-diagnostic
3: description: Read-only Jetson health snapshot for identity, memory, GPU, thermal, power, storage, services, and top processes.
4: version: 0.0.1
5: license: "Apache-2.0"

13: # Jetson Diagnostic
14: 
15: A unified, agent-friendly view of a running Jetson device. Replaces the need to remember which of `tegrastats`, `jtop`, `procrank`, `/sys/kernel/debug/nvmap`, `nvpmodel`, `free`, `swapon`, `df`, and `systemctl list-units` produces which slice of the truth.
16: 
17: ## Purpose
18: 
19: Capture a read-only health snapshot from the Jetson host so agents can answer device identity, memory, GPU, thermal, power, storage, and service-state questions using live data instead of guesses.
20: 
21: ## When to use
22: 
23: Activate when the user asks:
24: 
25: - "What is this Jetson? What SKU? How much memory?"
26: - "What's running on this Jetson right now?"
27: - "Why is my Jetson slow / hot / out of memory?"
28: - "Give me a snapshot of GPU / CPU / power usage."
29: - "What does my tegrastats output mean?"
30: - "Which services are running that I could turn off?"
31: - The user has installed `jetson-memory-audit`, `jetson-headless-mode`, `jetson-inference-mem-tune`, `jetson-llm-benchmark`, `jetson-llm-serve`, or `jetson-package` and needs a baseline measurement before running them.
32: 
33: Do not use this skill to change power modes, drop caches, stop services, install packages, serve models, or tune inference flags. Report the observed state, then hand off to the action-oriented skill.
34: 
35: ## Prerequisites
36: 
37: - Run on the Jetson host, or in a sandbox/container with host-visible Jetson system paths and process data.
38: 
39: ## Available Scripts
40: 
41: | Script | Purpose | Arguments |
42: |--------|---------|-----------|
43: | `scripts/snapshot.sh` | Emits the all-in-one JSON snapshot for identity, memory, GPU, thermal, power, disk, top processes, and candidate services. | `--human`, `--tegra-secs N`, `--top-procs N`. |
44: | `scripts/mem_summary.sh` | Emits a compact human-readable RAM/GPU/swap summary. | `--short`, `--watch`, `--interval N`. |
45: | `scripts/detect_jetson.sh` | Exports or prints canonical Jetson SKU/generation/product-line fields for this repo. | No arguments. |
46: 
47: If your agent runtime supports `run_script`, use it to run `scripts/snapshot.sh` or `scripts/mem_summary.sh` and summarize the returned output. Otherwise run the scripts with `bash` from the repository root.
48: 
49: ## Instructions
50: 
51: 1. Run `scripts/snapshot.sh` for the all-in-one JSON view (preferred default).
52: 2. For a quick human-readable memory line, run `scripts/mem_summary.sh`.
53: 3. To explain a single tegrastats line the user has pasted, see `references/tegrastats-fields.md`.
54: 4. To explain the NvMap clients output, see `references/nvmap-clients.md`.
55: 
56: ## Reporting guidance
57: 
58: Run the matching helper script before summarizing device state, and report only fields returned by that script. If direct execution is blocked by the runtime, run it with `bash {baseDir}/scripts/<script-name>` rather than trying to chmod files.
59: 
60: - For "what is this Jetson" questions, quote `product_model` or `sku`, `variant`, `l4t_version`, and `mem_total_gb`.
61: - For "slow and hot" questions, run `snapshot.sh` and summarize both sides of the symptom: `thermal_c` for heat, plus `top_processes`, `gpu_processes`, `nvmap.top_clients`, or `gpu_source` for load. End with a concrete handoff such as `jetson-memory-audit`, `jetson-headless-mode`, or `jetson-inference-mem-tune`.
62: - For "which process is using memory" questions, run `snapshot.sh` and name the leading process as `pid <number>`, `cmd`, and its `pss_kb` / MiB value. If NvMap GPU memory is the relevant signal, also quote `gpu_source` and the top `nvmap.top_clients` or `gpu_processes` entry.
63: 
64: If your agent runtime does not automatically execute helper scripts relative to this skill directory, resolve script paths with the AgentSkills `{baseDir}` placeholder:
65: 
66: ```bash
67: {baseDir}/scripts/snapshot.sh
68: {baseDir}/scripts/mem_summary.sh
69: ```
70: 
71: Do not call `jetson-diagnostic` as a tool name unless the runtime explicitly registers skills as callable tools; Agent Skills are normally instructions plus files, not direct tool functions.
72: 
73: All scripts source the canonical platform detector at `skills/jetson-diagnostic/scripts/detect_jetson.sh` (exports `JETSON_SKU`, `JETSON_GENERATION`, `JETSON_PRODUCT_LINE`, `JETSON_VARIANT`, `JETSON_MEM_GB`, `JETSON_L4T_VERSION`, `JETSON_PRODUCT_MODEL`). Other skills may source this detector rather than duplicating Jetson identification logic. Exits 2 with a remediation message off-platform.
74: 
75: ## Limitations
76: 
77: - Seeing this skill file does not guarantee access to Jetson host hardware. If `/proc/device-tree/model`, `/etc/nv_tegra_release`, `tegrastats`, `nvpmodel`, `nvidia-smi`, or `/sys/kernel/debug/nvmap` are missing inside a NemoClaw/OpenClaw sandbox, say the sandbox lacks Jetson host visibility and ask the user to run on the Jetson host or relaunch with a host-visible sandbox profile.
78: - NvMap debugfs often requires root, so unprivileged runs may report `gpu_source: "none"` or incomplete `nvmap` fields.
79: - This skill reports observed state only. Do not fabricate memory, GPU, thermal, service, or reclamation data when a tool is missing or inaccessible.
80: 
81: ## Error handling
82: 
83: - If a helper exits off-platform, report that the current environment is not a Jetson host or lacks host visibility; do not substitute generic Linux values.
84: - If `tegrastats`, `nvpmodel`, `nvidia-smi`, or NvMap debugfs are unavailable, preserve the corresponding `null`, `false`, or empty fields from the JSON and explain which signal is limited.
85: - If `snapshot.sh` emits malformed JSON, report the raw failure and rerun after fixing the helper output; do not hand-edit a synthetic device snapshot.
86: 
87: ## Output contract for `snapshot.sh`
88: 
89: ```json
90: {
91:   "sku": "orin-nano",
92:   "generation": "orin",
93:   "product_line": "orin-nano",
94:   "variant": "orin-nano-8gb",
95:   "mem_total_gb": 8,
96:   "l4t_version": "36.4.0",
97:   "product_model": "nvidia jetson orin nano developer kit",
98:   "memory_kb": { "total": 8123456, "available": 4123456, "swap_total": 0, "swap_free": 0, "cached": 1234567 },
99:   "tegrastats_sample": "RAM 4011/8138MB (lfb 8x4MB) ...",
100:   "thermal_c": { "CPU": 52.3, "GPU": 49.0, "AO": 47.0 },
101:   "power": { "nvpmodel_id": 0, "nvpmodel_name": "MAXN" },
102:   "disk": [ { "mount": "/", "used_pct": 41 } ],
103:   "gpu_source": "nvmap:iovmm-clients",
104:   "gpu_devices": [],
105:   "gpu_processes": [],
106:   "nvmap": {
107:     "readable": true,
108:     "total_kb": 654321,
109:     "stats_total_bytes": 669985280,
110:     "top_clients": [ { "pid": 1234, "cmd": "vlm-server", "kb": 524288 } ]
111:   },
112:   "top_processes": [ { "pid": 4321, "cmd": "vllm", "pss_kb": 4000000 } ],
113:   "candidate_services": { "gdm3": { "active": "inactive", "enabled": "disabled" } }
114: }
115: ```
116: 
117: `gpu_source` names the *specific* datum the skill used to attribute per-process GPU memory, so the caller can tell exactly what the numbers represent:
118: 
119: - `"nvidia-smi:compute-apps"` — per-process `used_memory` values from `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps`. Used on the unified `nvidia.ko` stack (Thor family today). Note: on this stack `nvidia-smi`'s *device-level* `memory.used` query returns `[N/A]` on some BSPs, which is why the skill sums the per-process list rather than reading a top-level total. The summed total appears in `gpu_processes[*].used_mib`.
120: - `"nvmap:iovmm-clients"` — per-process sizes from `/sys/kernel/debug/nvmap/iovmm/clients`. Used on the `nvgpu` stack (Orin family today), where `nvidia-smi` is a stub that returns `[N/A]` for every compute/memory query. Per-process entries appear in `nvmap.top_clients`; the kernel-side total is in `nvmap.total_kb` and (when readable) `nvmap.stats_total_bytes`.
121: - `"none"` — no authoritative source reachable. Typical when running unprivileged on an `nvgpu`-stack Jetson (debugfs under `/sys/kernel/debug/nvmap` needs `sudo`); rerun with `sudo` to populate the `nvmap` fields.
122: 
123: The agent should present the salient parts back to the user (SKU, available memory, top GPU consumer per `gpu_source`, hottest zone, power mode) and offer to drill into specifics (`top_processes`, `gpu_processes` / `nvmap`, `services`).
124: 
125: ## Safety
126: 
127: This skill is **read-only**. It does not change `nvpmodel`, does not run `jetson_clocks`, does not modify services. To act on findings, hand off to:
128: 
129: - `jetson-memory-audit` — focused memory snapshot + drop_caches verify loop
130: - `jetson-headless-mode` — disable GUI + auxiliary daemons (safe, reversible)
131: - `jetson-inference-mem-tune` — pick runtime + memory flags (vLLM / SGLang / llama.cpp / TensorRT Edge-LLM)
132: - `jetson-llm-serve` — vLLM and related GHCR images with Jetson defaults
133: - `jetson-llm-benchmark` — reproducible latency / throughput benchmarks
134: - `jetson-package` — GHCR + Jetson AI Lab PyPI indexes vs generic ARM wheels
135: 
136: ## Cross-platform behavior
137: 
138: | Family                | Variants the skill recognises                              | `tegrastats` | `nvidia-smi`          | `nvpmodel` | NvMap debugfs |
139: |-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------|------------|----------------|
140: | Jetson Thor           | `thor-t5000`, `thor-t4000`                                 | yes          | yes (full)            | yes        | yes (root)     |
141: | Jetson AGX Orin       | `orin-agx-64gb`, `orin-agx-32gb`, `orin-agx-industrial`    | yes          | yes (stub, `nvgpu`)*  | yes        | yes (root)     |
142: | Jetson Orin NX        | `orin-nx-16gb`, `orin-nx-8gb`                              | yes          | yes (stub, `nvgpu`)*  | yes        | yes (root)     |
143: | Jetson Orin Nano      | `orin-nano-8gb`, `orin-nano-4gb`                           | yes          | yes (stub, `nvgpu`)*  | yes        | yes (root)     |
144: 
145: \* On Jetsons whose GPU is driven by the in-tree `nvgpu` kernel driver, the `nvidia-smi` binary is present but most fields (`Memory-Usage`, power, utilisation, compute-process table) report `Not Supported` / `N/A`. To decide which source to trust at runtime, the script does a capability probe — `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv,noheader,nounits` — and only uses `nvidia-smi` for per-process GPU memory when that query returns a real integer. When it doesn't, the script falls back to `/sys/kernel/debug/nvmap/iovmm/clients`, which on `nvgpu`-stack Jetsons is the authoritative per-process GPU-memory source.
146: 
147: The script handles each tool's presence gracefully and reports `null` / `false` for tools it cannot reach (typical when the agent isn't running with the privilege needed for `/sys/kernel/debug`). 2: 
3: > **Which source to trust for per-process GPU memory on Jetson**
4: >
5: > Run once: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv,noheader,nounits`.
6: > - If that prints a plain integer, the device is on the unified `nvidia.ko`
7: >   compute-driver stack. `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory`
8: >   is the authoritative per-process GPU-memory source. Under that stack
9: >   `iovmm/clients` will typically show `0K` for every row even under heavy CUDA
10: >   load, because CUDA allocations bypass nvmap.
11: > - If that prints `[N/A]`, `Not Supported`, or is empty, the device is on the
12: >   `nvgpu` in-tree driver. `nvidia-smi` is a stub and cannot report
13: >   Memory-Usage or compute processes; **this file** is the authoritative
14: >   per-process GPU-memory source.
15: >
16: > The skill's `scripts/snapshot.sh` picks the right source automatically with
17: > that one capability probe; no SKU or BSP check.
18: 
19: NvMap is the kernel allocator that backs CUDA, multimedia buffers (NVENC/NVDEC, V4L2, libargus), and accelerator surfaces on Jetsons running the `nvgpu` driver. Per-process accounting is exposed at:
20: 
21: ```bash
22: sudo cat /sys/kernel/debug/nvmap/iovmm/clients
23: ```
24: 
25: ## Example
26: 
27: ```
28: CLIENT                        PROCESS                PID    SIZE
29: user                          gnome-shell           1543    220K
30: user                          Xorg                  1234    180K
31: user                          vlm-server            4321    524288K
32: total                                                       524688K
33: ```
34: 
35: ## Field meanings
36: 
37: | Column     | Meaning                                                                          |
38: |------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
39: | `CLIENT`   | NvMap client class. `user` = user-space process. Kernel clients also appear.     |
40: | `PROCESS`  | Process name (kernel `comm`).                                                    |
41: | `PID`      | Process ID.                                                                      |
42: | `SIZE`     | Bytes (suffixed `K`/`M`) currently allocated through NvMap.                      |
43: | `total`    | Sum across all clients. The most useful single number on this page.              |
44: 
45: ## Why NvMap matters
46: 
47: On Jetson, **CPU-side and GPU/multimedia memory share the same physical pool**. A process that allocates a giant CUDA tensor or a chain of NVDEC surfaces will not show that memory in `/proc/[pid]/status` (RSS) or `top`, but it _will_ show it here. If `free -m` says memory is full and `top` cannot account for it, NvMap is the next stop.
48: 
49: ## Quick triage
50: 
51: - **Total NvMap >= 50% of system memory** → graphics / multimedia / CUDA is the dominant consumer; see [tegrastats-fields.md](tegrastats-fields.md) `GR3D_FREQ`.
52: - **GUI processes (`gnome-shell`, `Xorg`) holding non-trivial NvMap** → headless mode would reclaim it. See `jetson-headless-mode`.
53: - **One inference process holding most of the total** → likely model weights + KV cache. Tune the runtime (smaller batch, smaller context, lower precision). See `jetson-inference-mem-tune`.
54: - **A dead container or stale `python3` holding NvMap** → reap it; container teardown sometimes leaks GPU surfaces.
55: 
56: ## Permissions
57: 
58: `debugfs` is root-readable. Agents running unprivileged will see "Permission denied". Either run with `sudo` or add a small `sudo`-rules entry for the diagnostic command.
59: 
60: ## Per-client view
61: 
62: For a richer breakdown (per-allocation, with backtraces) see:
63: 
64: ```bash
65: sudo cat /sys/kernel/debug/nvmap/iovmm/allocations
66: ```
67: 
68: Verbose; use only when triaging a specific leak.", "references/tegrastats-fields.md": "1: # Reading `tegrastats` output
2: 
3: `tegrastats` is the canonical Jetson telemetry tool. **Output tokens and spelling change across Jetson Linux / L4T releases and SoCs** (for example older guides document `EMC X%@Y` while newer Orin/Thor guides document `EMC_FREQ` with several alternate shapes). Treat any single cheat-sheet as approximate.
4: 
5: **There is no single NVIDIA table that covers every minor Jetson Linux revision.** The **Reported Statistics** glossary can differ between nearby releases (for example **R38.2.x vs R38.4.0**). Prefer the archive whose **Jetson Linux version string** best matches `cat /etc/nv_tegra_release` on the device; if NVIDIA has not published that exact slug, use the **closest published** archive for your product line and still sanity-check against live `tegrastats` output.
6: 
7: ## Official documentation (NVIDIA)
8: 
9: The authoritative field glossary and CLI options live in the **Jetson Linux Developer Guide**, topic **Tegrastats Utility** (under *Applications and Tools → Jetson Linux Development Tools*). The HTML basename is stable:
10: 
11: `DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html`
12: 
13: ### URL pattern
14: 
15: Substitute the archive folder name (Jetson Linux release) for `<SLUG>`:
16: 
17: `https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/<SLUG>/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html`
18: 
19: Browse NVIDIA’s [Jetson documentation archives](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/) to find the `<SLUG>` that matches your image (for example `r38.4`, `r36.4.4`). Not every **minor** gets its own folder (for example **`r38.2.2` and `r38.4.0` may 404** while **`r38.2.1`** and **`r38.4`** exist); use the nearest published slug.
20: 
21: ### Per-archive **Tegrastats Utility** pages (known-good slugs)
22: 
23: The links below were **spot-checked** (HTTP `200`); NVIDIA may add or retire archive folders over time — if one fails, use the [archives index](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/) and the URL pattern above.
24: 
25: | Archive slug | Tegrastats Utility (Reported Statistics) |
26: |--------------|------------------------------------------|
27: | `r35.5.0` | [Tegrastats Utility — r35.5.0](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r35.5.0/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
28: | `r35.6.4` | [Tegrastats Utility — r35.6.4](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r35.6.4/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
29: | `r36.2` | [Tegrastats Utility — r36.2](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.2/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
30: | `r36.3` | [Tegrastats Utility — r36.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.3/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
31: | `r36.4.3` | [Tegrastats Utility — r36.4.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.4.3/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
32: | `r36.4.4` | [Tegrastats Utility — r36.4.4](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.4.4/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
33: | `r36.5` | [Tegrastats Utility — r36.5](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.5/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
34: | `r38.2` | [Tegrastats Utility — r38.2](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r38.2/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
35: | `r38.2.1` | [Tegrastats Utility — r38.2.1](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r38.2.1/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
36: | `r38.4` | [Tegrastats Utility — r38.4](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r38.4/DeveloperGuide/AT/JetsonLinuxDevelopmentTools/TegrastatsUtility.html) |
37: 
38: **Welcome** indices (overview only, not the field table): [r38.4](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r38.4/DeveloperGuide/index.html), [r36.5](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r36.5/DeveloperGuide/index.html), [r35.6.4](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r35.6.4/DeveloperGuide/index.html).
39: 
40: Welcome-only context: Jetson Linux **38.2** documentation explicitly states that release **does not support the Jetson Orin product family** at GA time; use a **36.x** guide for Orin-focused `tegrastats` wording when that applies to your stack ([r38.2 Welcome](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/r38.2/DeveloperGuide/index.html)).
41: 
42: ### Man page?
43: 
44: Many images ship **`tegrastats` without a `man` page**; use `tegrastats --help` on the device for a short option list, and the **Tegrastats Utility** topic for full semantics. NVIDIA also documents the binary location as `/core/utils/tegrastats` in the BSP package layout.
45: 
46: ### Very old Jetson Linux (e.g. L4T 32.x)
47: 
48: Archived L4T help bundles (such as [Jetson Linux 32.7.6](https://docs.nvidia.com/jetson/archives/l4t-archived/l4t-3276/index.html)) may use an older web help shell; if search fails, use the PDF/HTML **Development Guide** for that release from the [Jetson Download Center](https://developer.nvidia.com/embedded/downloads) or cross-check a nearby **r35.x** archive link above.
49:
